subject: Clarify math: rounding / billing-unit behavior for mixed prompt+streamed responses

Subject: Clarify rounding behavior for our quote (RWD-2026-BS-47)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the fast follow-up on the SOW. Procurement had a few quick, practical questions about how Redwood counts/bills tokens so our finance team can reconcile against our internal cost model before we route the PO. Specifically: 

1) Is the billable quantity computed as exact token counts (prompt + generated) or do you round up to a billing unit per request? If you round, what's the unit size and is it per HTTP request or aggregated per minute/customer?

2) For streaming responses, do you bill partial streamed chunks as they emit, or only the final token tally when the stream is closed?

3) How do minimums apply? Our use case has many short prompts (~20–60 tokens) and occasional long-generation flows (2k+ tokens). Will those short prompts get hit by a per-request minimum that materially increases costs?

Attached the latest SOW and the pricing sheet we want to match against. Can you give two numeric examples (one short-turn prompt, one long prompt) showing how the math works with rounding and our 25% committed discount?

Thanks — Sarah

Subject: Re: Clarify rounding behavior for our quote (RWD-2026-BS-47)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note. Quick summary up front, then two worked examples as requested.

Short answer (what we applied on the quote):
- Canonical token accounting: billable_tokens = prompt_tokens + generated_tokens (we count tokens exactly).
- To keep invoices simple for committed customers we convert billable_tokens into "billing units" where 1 billing unit = 50 tokens for your quoted plan. The invoice shows units; the math uses CEIL(total_tokens / 50) * 50 to compute billed tokens.
- The unit rounding applies per request for Hosted API calls (HTTP request boundary). For Dedicated/reserved capacity customers we round at the invoice aggregation stage (monthly sum) to the nearest 100 tokens because billing is per-commit.
- Streaming: we bill based on tokens actually generated; streaming does not create extra rounding while partial chunks are emitted. The request-level rounding happens at the end of the request when the final token tally is known.
- Minimums: we do NOT have a separate per-request fixed minimum on your plan beyond the billing-unit rounding. So a 12-token prompt + 8-token response is billed as CEIL(20/50)*50 = 50 tokens. That is the behavior quoted.

Worked examples (with your 25% committed discount applied on the billed token cost):
Assumptions in the quote: price_per_1k_tokens = $1.20 (list), committed_discount = 25% -> effective price = $0.90 / 1k tokens = $0.0009 / token. Billing unit = 50 tokens.

Example 1 — short-turn prompt:
- prompt_tokens = 12, generated_tokens = 28 -> total = 40 tokens
- billed_tokens = CEIL(40 / 50) * 50 = 50 tokens
- cost = 50 * $0.0009 = $0.045 -> invoice will show 1 unit (50 tokens) = $0.045

Example 2 — long generation:
- prompt_tokens = 980, generated_tokens = 1020 -> total = 2000 tokens
- billed_tokens = CEIL(2000 / 50) * 50 = 2000 tokens (already aligned)
- cost = 2000 * $0.0009 = $1.80

Notes and corner cases:
- If you stream a response and the client cancels mid-stream, we bill only the tokens actually emitted up to cancel; rounding still applies to the final token count for that request.
- For bursty environments where you make many tiny requests we can offer a per-request minimum override in enterprise SOWs (e.g., flat per-request min of 20 units) if you prefer simpler forecasting — this would be written into the SOW and affects the example math.
- For Dedicated customers who buy committed capacity, the invoice-level rounding uses a 100-token unit, and we reconcile usage vs commit monthly; overage rates are the same unit price but applied to the reconciled billed units.

I've attached a copy of the pricing_calc_sheet with the same examples so your finance team can drop in their volumes.

If that matches what you need, I'll update the SOW language to explicitly call out the 50-token billing unit and the streaming/cancellation behavior.

Thanks Marissa — that helps a lot. Two quick follow-ups: 
1) For the streaming cancellation case, can you confirm whether tokens emitted in the same HTTP request but across multiple stream frames are considered a single request for rounding? (i.e., do we get charged just once using CEIL(final_count/50) or could intermediate accounting ever cause us to pay more?)
2) For the committed discount proration: if we sign mid-month, is the commit prorated daily and the discount applied pro-rata?

If you can add two lines to the SOW that read: "Billing units: 50 tokens; per-request rounding as CEIL(total_tokens/50)*50; streaming billed on final token count; committed discount prorated daily on sign date" we'll be comfortable moving the PO to procurement.

—Sarah

Subject: Re: Clarify rounding behavior for our quote (RWD-2026-BS-47)

Sarah — quick technical confirmation from infra: streaming frames within a single request are aggregated server-side; the billable token tally is the final token count at request close. There is no interim invoiceable event for partial frames.

Marissa — procurement proration is handled by Finance: commit discounts prorate on a daily basis from your sign date; the invoiced discount for the first month will be proportional to the days covered by the committed period. I'll confirm exact prorata calc (Finance uses calendar-day proration) and Marissa can include a short sentence in the SOW.

I'll also drop a DocuSign link for the SOW once Marissa confirms the two SOW sentences.
